name: application-range-inputs
title: Range Inputs
description: Slider controls for selecting a value within a continuous numeric range, used for volume, brightness, price filters, and tolerance settings.
useWhen: Users need to select a value within a continuous numeric range, such as volume or brightness.
Filtering by a price range or distance in a search interface.
Setting a tolerance or threshold that can be tuned rather than typed precisely.
avoidWhen: An exact numeric value is required — a number input is more precise and easier to keyboard-navigate.
The value has only a few discrete steps — radio buttons or a segmented control communicate the options more clearly.
Users need to set both a minimum and maximum bound simultaneously — implement a dual-handle range slider.
responsiveBehavior: Range sliders fill their container width. Track and thumb sizes should be large enough for comfortable touch interaction without additional styling.
accessibility: Use the native <input type='range'> element so keyboard users can adjust the value with arrow keys.
Link a visible <label> to the range input; display the current value in an adjacent <output> element.
Provide min, max, and step attributes so screen readers can announce the full context.

variants.title: Base
variants.description: Simple horizontal range slider with no visible value label, for contexts where the current value is communicated elsewhere.
accessibility: Must have a linked label; consider pairing with an <output> to display the current value.

variants.title: Base with output
variants.description: Range slider with a live numeric output that updates as the user drags the thumb.
accessibility: The <output> element updates in real time and is announced by screen readers on change.

variants.title: Base with min and max labels
variants.description: Range slider with fixed min and max text labels at each end of the track to communicate the value boundaries.
accessibility: End labels are informational; the input's min and max attributes communicate boundaries programmatically.

variants.title: Native with tick marks
variants.description: Browser-native range slider with a <datalist> providing visible tick marks at interval positions.
accessibility: Tick marks are rendered by the browser; <datalist> option values snap the slider to available positions.

variants.title: Native with label marks
variants.description: Range slider with a <datalist> providing both tick marks and visible text labels below each stop.
accessibility: Label text below tick marks supplements the slider; the <datalist> IDs remain the accessible reference.
